g.text: Cross-Network Meta-Learning Gate for Monthly Rainfall Forecast Combination

g.text: Australia, SILO (gauge observations)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #2e7d32

g.text: Indonesia, NASA POWER (reanalysis-based grid)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: preprocessing

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 1. Rainfall preprocessing
Daily rainfall, 15 stations, 1926–2025 → monthly totals (1,200 months)
Validity mask: month valid if ≥ 90% of days have an observation code
(SILO codes 0, 13, 15, 23); invalid months = inputs only, never targets
Two stations without observed test months are excluded from evaluation

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 1. Rainfall preprocessing
Daily PRECTOTCORR, 20 city coordinates, 1981–2025 → monthly
totals (540 months); no missing days, mask trivially true
Monthly totals reconciled with the source monthly files
(difference < 0.05 mm); all 20 locations evaluated

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: indices

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 2. Climate-index predictors with release latency
Niño3.4 (ERSST v5), DMI (HadISST), SOI (CRU), monthly
Row t holds only values known at the end of month t:
SST indices up to t − 1, SOI up to t
Anomaly baseline 1926–1960; standardised with pre-2010 data only

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 2. Climate-index predictors with release latency
Niño3.4, Niño4, DMI, SOI, MJO RMM1, RMM2 (monthly means)
SST indices up to t − 1, SOI and RMM up to t
Niño anomalies re-referenced to 1981–1995 (causal baseline)
Standardised with pre-2013 data only

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: base models

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 3. Base-model pool, rolling retraining
9 models per station: SARIMA, SVR, XGBoost, LSTM, GRU,
XGBoost-VMD, XGBoost-WT, LSTM-VMD, LSTM-WT
Initial training 1941–1960; refit every 5 years 1961–2021 (13×)
+ expanding and 30-year rolling climatologies → 11-member pool
Forecasts every month, h = 1, 3, 6, 12; VMD recomputed per origin, 21.3 min

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 3. Base-model pool, rolling retraining
Same 9 models and hyperparameters
Initial training 1983–1995; refit every 5 years 1996–2021 (6×)
+ expanding and 20-year rolling climatologies → 11-member pool
Forecasts every month, h = 1, 3, 6, 12; decompositions causal, 10.6 min

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: meta-dataset

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 4. Meta-dataset and per-network gates
Per (station, origin o, horizon h): E = 12-month scaled error history
(12 × 11, targets ≤ o − 1), member forecasts p, sin–cos month,
6 regime features, one-hot h, target, all divided by σ_station (pre-2010)
Split: meta-train 1962–2009 / validation 2010–2014 / test 2015–2025
Gates trained here: L-G3, L-G4 (local), GG3, GG4 (global), GG4-T (transfer), 5.0 min

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 4. Meta-dataset and per-network gates
Same meta-sample structure; 6 regime features = latest values
of the 6 indices; σ_station from pre-2013 data
Split: meta-train 1997–2012 / validation 2013–2017 / test 2018–2025
Gates trained here: L-G3, L-G4, GG3, GG4, GG4-T, 2.8 min

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: harmonisation

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 5. Harmonisation into one joint meta-dataset: 72,520 meta-samples, 35 stations
• Pool aligned by position: 9 base models + expanding climatology + windowed climatology (30 yr AU / 20 yr ID treated as one member type)
• Regime features reduced to the 3 indices shared by both networks (Niño3.4, DMI, SOI), each kept standardised with its own region's pre-validation data (causal)
• 6 static station features (sin lat, sin/cos lon, log annual rainfall, annual-harmonic amplitude, timing of wettest month) recomputed from pre-validation data, standardised over 35 stations
• σ-scaling already makes E, p, y comparable across networks (150 mm/yr Woomera … 3,500 mm/yr Pontianak)
• Time-split labels and row order kept per network, so the stage-4 gate predictions map onto the joint dataset by a row offset

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: gates

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 6. Gates: one shared architecture, 3 seeds each
LSTM-16 over E ⊕ p ⊕ month ⊕ 3 regime features ⊕ horizon [⊕ station embedding ⊕ static features]
→ dense-16 (ReLU, dropout 0.2) → logits [+ NNLS log-prior anchor] → softmax weights w → ŷ = Σ w·p
Adam 10⁻³, MSE on scaled targets, L2, early stopping (patience 30, region validation sets), batch 256
RG region-only control: one region, harmonised 3-index features, embedding + static → isolates pooling from feature change
JG-E joint gate, 35 stations, embedding + static → analogue of GG3 on the pooled network
JG-S joint gate, static features only (no embedding) → applicable to unseen stations
LRO leave-region-out: trained on one network only (no embedding, anchor from that network) → zero-shot on the other
Scale LRO-type gates trained on k = 4, 8, 14, 28 random stations (5 draws), tested on 7 fixed holdout stations (3 AU + 4 ID)
22 configurations x 3 seeds, 3.0 min

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: Hypotheses fixed before the run
H1 JG-E ≥ RG in both regions
(pooling across networks does not hurt,
helps at ≥ 1 horizon per region)
H2 LRO ≥ L-G3 of the target network
(zero-shot gate beats local gates)
H3 LRO ≈ GG4-T of the target network
(exploratory)
H4 holdout NSE rises with k
(exploratory)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #ffffff

g.text: evaluation

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 7. Evaluation: each network in its own test period, against its own benchmarks
Benchmarks: the stage-4 gates L-G3, L-G4, GG3, GG4, GG4-T · NNLS per station–horizon (pre-test)
· simple mean · windowed climatology · best pre-test base model
Accuracy: NSE per station / horizon / period (AU 2015–2025, ID 2018–2025, each with two sub-periods), RMSE, MAE
Tests: DM-HLN per station–horizon, Holm within region (52 AU / 80 ID) · panel DM per region on cross-station mean
loss differentials, Holm over 4 horizons, squared and absolute errors · wins / median MSE change
Scaling curve: holdout NSE vs k (mean ± sd over draws) vs L-G3 and GG4-T on the same stations
Weight composition of the joint gate per model family, network, and horizon

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: 8. Outputs
regions/<network>/: raw and processed
data, base models, meta-dataset,
per-network gates
results/: the 22 cross-network gates,
evaluation_results.json
reports/: Tables 1–4, Figures 1–4
notebooks/: executed notebook
README with the main results

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #263238

g.text: Anti-leakage guarantees carried through every stage
Inputs precede the forecast origin (release latency, causal VMD/wavelet, error history ≤ o − 1) · σ, climatologies, static features, and index standardisation from pre-validation data only
NNLS anchors of LRO / scaling gates from training stations only · holdout stations never in training or validation · no hyperparameter tuned on any test period
Each test period touched once per configuration · hypotheses written down before the first gate was trained
